{{2000 Summer Olympics}}

The [[2000 Summer Olympics]], officially known as the Games of the XXVII Olympiad, were a summer [[multi-sport event]] held in [[Sydney]], [[New South Wales]], Australia, from 15 September to 1 October 2000.<ref name="EBEntry">{{cite encyclopedia |title=Sydney 2000 Olympic Games |encyclopedia=[[Encyclopædia Britannica]] |url=https://www.britannica.com/event/Sydney-2000-Olympic-Games |access-date=24 December 2024 |last=Johnston |first=Mindy |date=8 September 2024 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200707142704/https://www.britannica.com/event/Sydney-2000-Olympic-Games |archive-date=7 July 2020}}</ref> A total of 10,651&nbsp;athletes from 199&nbsp;nations represented by [[National Olympic Committee]]s (NOCs) (with [[Individual Olympic Athletes at the 2000 Summer Olympics|four individual athletes]] from [[East Timor]] because the country had no NOC),<ref name=olympicsorg>{{cite web|url=http://www.olympic.org/en/content/Olympic-Games/All-Past-Olympic-Games/Summer/Sydney-2000/|title=Sydney 2000|access-date=2008-07-15|publisher=International Olympic Committee|archive-date=25 December 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181225174238/https://www.olympic.org/sydney-2000|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name=GuardianOpening/> including the Olympic debuts of [[Eritrea at the 2000 Summer Olympics|Eritrea]], [[Federated States of Micronesia at the 2000 Summer Olympics|Micronesia]] and [[Palau at the 2000 Summer Olympics|Palau]].<ref name=GuardianOpening>{{cite news|last=Engel|first=Matthew|title=An Olympics to fire the flames of optimism|url=https://www.theguardian.com/Columnists/Column/0,5673,369170,00.html|work=[[The Guardian]]|date=16 September 2000|access-date=24 September 2024}}</ref> The games featured 300 events in 28 [[Olympic sports|sports]] across 39 disciplines,<ref name=olympicsorg/><ref>{{cite web|title=2000 Summer Olympics|url=https://www.olympedia.org/editions/25|work=Olympedia|access-date=24 September 2024}}</ref> including the debuts of [[Diving at the Summer Olympics|synchronized diving]], [[Taekwondo at the Summer Olympics|taekwondo]],  [[Triathlon at the Summer Olympics|triathlon]], [[Gymnastics at the Summer Olympics|trampolining]], women's [[Modern pentathlon at the Summer Olympics|modern pentathlon]] and women's [[Weightlifting at the Summer Olympics|weightlifting]] as official Olympic medal events.<ref name=EBEntry/><ref name="olympicsorg" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Taekwondo |url=https://www.olympedia.org/sports/TKW |access-date=24 December 2024 |website=Olympedia}}</ref>

Athletes from 80&nbsp;countries won at least one medal, a new record,<ref>{{cite web|title=Sydney 2000|date=10 August 2011 |url=https://olympic.ca/games/2000-sydney/|publisher=[[Canadian Olympic Committee]]|access-date=25 September 2024}}</ref> with 52 nations winning at least one gold medal.<ref name=IOCMedals/> The [[United States at the 2000 Summer Olympics|United States]] won the most gold medals, with 37, and the most medals overall, with 93.<ref name=IOCMedals/> It was the second consecutive Summer Olympic Games that the United States led the medal count in both gold and overall medals.<ref>{{cite news|last=Livengood|first=Paul|title=Does the United States always win the medal count? Here's a look at every Summer Olympics final medal count in history|url=https://www.wfaa.com/article/sports/olympics/olympic-medal-count-paris-usa-history/287-856b12a9-cc80-4534-bb36-ff3442e5ce7e|publisher=[[WFAA]]|date=8 August 2024|access-date=25 September 2024}}</ref> Host nation [[Australia at the 2000 Summer Olympics|Australia]] finished the Games with 58 medals overall (16&nbsp;gold, 25&nbsp;silver, and 17&nbsp;bronze).<ref>{{cite news|last=Tancred|first=Mike|title=Sydney 2000 Olympics remembered for national pride and goodwill|url=https://www.smh.com.au/sport/sydney-2000-olympics-remembered-for-national-pride-and-goodwill-20150912-gjl8dt.html|work=[[The Sydney Morning Herald]]|date=12 September 2015|access-date=25 September 2024|archive-date=25 September 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240925200755/https://www.smh.com.au/sport/sydney-2000-olympics-remembered-for-national-pride-and-goodwill-20150912-gjl8dt.html|url-status=live}}</ref> [[Cameroon]],<ref>{{cite news|title=Sydney 2000: Soccer; After Furious Draw, Cameroon Is Golden|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2000/09/30/sports/sydney-2000-soccer-after-furious-draw-cameroon-is-golden.html|work=[[The New York Times]]|agency=[[Reuters]]|date=30 September 2000|access-date=25 September 2024|url-access=subscription}}</ref> [[Colombia]],<ref>{{cite news|last=Buckley|first=Will|title=Maria whistles to glory|url=https://www.theguardian.com/observer/sport/story/0,6903,372568,00.html|work=[[The Guardian]]|date=24 September 2000|access-date=25 September 2024}}</ref> [[Latvia]],<ref>{{cite news|last=Zariņš|first=Viesturs|title=Who will bring home Olympic medals for Latvia?|url=https://latviansonline.com/who-will-bring-home-olympic-medals-for-latvia/|work=Latvians Online|date=29 July 2012|access-date=25 September 2024|archive-date=25 September 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240925142416/https://latviansonline.com/who-will-bring-home-olympic-medals-for-latvia/|url-status=live}}</ref> [[Mozambique]]<ref>{{cite journal|last=Boavida|first=Maria|title=Maria Mutola – The Running Wonder from Mozambique|url=https://unesdoc.unesco.org/ark:/48223/pf0000191795|journal=[[UNESCO Courier]]|date=September 2006|pages=12–13|access-date=25 September 2024}}</ref> and [[Slovenia]] won a gold medal for the first time in their Olympic histories,<ref>{{cite news|last=Smrdel|first=Tania|title=20 years since Summer Olympic games in Sydney|url=https://www.sbs.com.au/language/slovenian/en/podcast-episode/20-years-since-summer-olympic-games-in-sydney/75omzw8z8|publisher=[[Special Broadcasting Service]]|date=26 September 2020|access-date=25 September 2024}}</ref> while [[Vietnam]],<ref>{{cite news|last=Murray|first=Shane|title=Olympics: Vietnam hails first ever medallist|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/2000/0929/151733-olympics1/|publisher=[[RTÉ Sport]]|agency=[[Reuters]]|date=29 September 2000|access-date=25 September 2024}}</ref> [[Barbados]],<ref>{{cite news|title=Thousands welcome Obadele Thompson home|url=https://worldathletics.org/news/news/thousands-welcome-obadele-thompson-home|publisher=[[World Athletics]]|agency=[[Reuters]]|date=8 October 2000|access-date=25 September 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231118010807/https://worldathletics.org/news/news/thousands-welcome-obadele-thompson-home|archive-date=18 November 2023|url-status=dead}}</ref> [[North Macedonia|Macedonia]],<ref>{{cite news|title=On this day, Ibragimov brought the first Olympic medal for Macedonia!|url=https://www.slobodenpecat.mk/en/na-deneshen-den-ibragimov-go-donese-prviot-olimpiski-medal-za-makedonija-video/|work=[[Sloboden Pečat]]|date=1 October 2020|access-date=25 September 2024}}</ref> [[Kuwait]],<ref>{{cite news|title=First Olympic Medal for Kuwait|url=https://www.kuna.net.kw/ArticleDetails.aspx?id=1111316&language=en|agency=[[Kuwait News Agency]]|date=20 September 2000|access-date=25 September 2024}}</ref> [[Kyrgyzstan]],<ref>{{cite web|last=Brennan|first=Eliott|title=Kyrgyzstan NOC pays tribute to athletes on Independence Day|url=https://www.insidethegames.biz/articles/1127595/kyrgyzstan-noc-independence-day|work=[[Inside the Games]]|date=2 September 2022|access-date=25 September 2024}}</ref> and [[Saudi Arabia]] won their first ever Olympic medals.<ref>{{cite web|last=Alomar|first=Dana|title=A history of Saudi Arabia at the Olympic Games|url=https://www.esquireme.com/sports/54168-a-history-of-saudi-arabia-at-the-olympic-games|work=[[Esquire (magazine)|Esquire Middle East]]|date=21 July 2021|access-date=25 September 2024}}</ref> Among individual athletes, Australia's [[Ian Thorpe]], the Netherlands' [[Leontien van Moorsel]] and [[Inge de Bruijn]] and the United States' [[Jenny Thompson]] and [[Lenny Krayzelburg]] won the most gold medals at the games with three each and Russian gymnast [[Alexei Nemov]] won the most overall medals with six (two gold, one silver and three bronze).<ref name=SR2000>{{cite web|title=2000 Sydney Summer Games|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/summer/2000/|work=[[Sports Reference]]|access-date=24 September 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200114073017/https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/summer/2000/|archive-date=14 January 2020|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Medal table==
{{See also|Olympic medal table}}

The medal table is based on information provided by the [[International Olympic Committee]] (IOC) and is consistent with IOC conventional sorting in its published medal tables.<ref name=olympicsorg/> The table uses the [[Olympic medal table]] sorting method. By default, the table is ordered by the number of gold medals the athletes from a nation have won, where a nation is an entity represented by a NOC. The number of silver medals is taken into consideration next and then the number of bronze medals.<ref>{{cite news |title=Olympic medal table: USA beat China to top spot at Paris 2024 |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/olympics/olympics-2024-medal-table-count-paris-b2580716.html |work=[[The Independent]] | date=11 August 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240812015233/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/olympics/olympics-2024-medal-table-count-paris-b2594580.html |archive-date=12 August 2024 |url-status=live |last1=Ostlere |first1=Lawrence |access-date=12 August 2024 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=A Medal Count That Adds Up To Little |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2008/08/19/sports/olympics/19araton.html |work=[[The New York Times]] | date=18 August 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230321004238/https://www.nytimes.com/2008/08/19/sports/olympics/19araton.html |archive-date=21 March 2023 |url-status=live |last1=Araton |first1=Harvey |url-access=subscription |access-date=25 July 2024 }}</ref> If teams are still tied, equal ranking is given and they are listed alphabetically by their [[List of IOC country codes|IOC country code]].<ref>{{cite news |title=What happens if two countries are tied in the Olympic medal table? Tiebreaker rules explained |url=https://en.as.com/olympic_games/what-happens-if-two-countries-are-tied-in-the-olympic-medal-table-tiebreaker-rules-explained-n/ |work=[[Diario AS]] |date=10 August 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240811152350/https://en.as.com/olympic_games/what-happens-if-two-countries-are-tied-in-the-olympic-medal-table-tiebreaker-rules-explained-n/ |archive-date=August 11, 2024 |url-status=live |last1=Cons |first1=Roddy |access-date=11 August 2024 |language=en-us }}</ref>

Events in [[Boxing at the 2000 Summer Olympics|boxing]] result in a bronze medal being awarded to each of the two competitors who lose their semi-final matches, as opposed to fighting in a [[Third place playoff|third place tie breaker]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Explained: Two bronze medals are awarded in the Olympics boxing competition |url=https://olympics.com/en/news/why-two-bronze-medals-boxing |publisher=[[International Olympic Committee]] | date=1 August 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230328143327/https://olympics.com/en/news/why-two-bronze-medals-boxing |archive-date=28 March 2023 |url-status=live |last1=Ansari |first1=Aarish |access-date=25 September 2024 }}</ref> Another combat sport, [[Judo at the 2000 Summer Olympics|judo]], uses a [[repechage system]] which also results in two bronze medals being awarded.<ref>{{cite web |title=Repechage in wrestling and other sports explained – the second chance |url=https://olympics.com/en/news/what-is-repechage-rules |publisher=[[International Olympic Committee]] | date=21 June 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240802015913/https://olympics.com/en/news/what-is-repechage-rules |archive-date=2 August 2024 |url-status=live |last1=Nag |first1=Utathya |access-date=25 September 2024 }}</ref>

There were two ties for medals in athletics. No gold medal and two silver medals were awarded due to second-place ties in the [[Athletics at the 2000 Summer Olympics – Women's 100 metres|women's 100 metres]] while a tie for third place in the [[Athletics at the 2000 Summer Olympics – Women's high jump|women's high jump]] saw two bronze medals being awarded.<ref>{{cite web|title=Athletics at the 2000 Sydney Summer Games: Women's 100 metres|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/summer/2000/ATH/womens-100-metres.html|work=[[Sports Reference]]|access-date=25 September 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200417173401/https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/summer/2000/ATH/womens-100-metres.html|archive-date=17 April 2020|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Athletics at the 2000 Sydney Summer Games: Women's High Jump|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/summer/2000/ATH/womens-high-jump.html|work=[[Sports Reference]]|access-date=25 September 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200417174250/https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/summer/2000/ATH/womens-high-jump.html|archive-date=17 April 2020|url-status=dead}}</ref> In swimming events, there were two more ties for medals. There was a two-way tie for first place in the [[Swimming at the 2000 Summer Olympics – Men's 50 metre freestyle|men's 50 metre freestyle]], which resulted in two gold medals and no silver medals being awarded.<ref>{{cite web|title=Sydney 2000 Swimming 50m Freestyle Men Results|url=https://olympics.com/en/olympic-games/sydney-2000/results/swimming/50m-freestyle-men|publisher=[[International Olympic Committee]]|access-date=25 September 2024}}</ref> Two bronze medals were awarded in the [[Swimming at the 2000 Summer Olympics – Women's 100 metre freestyle|women's 100 metre freestyle]] due to a tie for third place.<ref>{{cite web|title=Sydney 2000 Swimming 100m Freestyle Women Results|url=https://olympics.com/en/olympic-games/sydney-2000/results/swimming/100m-freestyle-women|publisher=[[International Olympic Committee]]|access-date=25 September 2024}}</ref>

| rowspan=4 align=left | Three weeks after the games, [[Alexander Leipold]] of [[Germany at the 2000 Summer Olympics|Germany]] was stripped of his gold medal after he tested positive for [[nandrolone]], with the medal being reallocated to his [[United States at the 2000 Summer Olympics|American]] rival, originally second-placed [[Brandon Slay]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://abcnews.go.com/Sports/story?id=100259&page=1|title=IOC Strips Leipold of Wrestling Gold|date=23 October 2000|work=[[ABC News (United States)|ABC News]]|access-date=11 May 2012|archive-date=31 January 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110131003141/http://abcnews.go.com/Sports/story?id=100259&page=1|url-status=live}}</ref>

! scope="rowgroup" rowspan=11 | 5 October 2007
| rowspan=3 | [[Athletics at the 2000 Summer Olympics|Athletics]], [[Athletics at the 2000 Summer Olympics – Women's 100 metres|Women's 100 metres]]
| align=left | {{flagIOCathlete|[[Marion Jones]]|USA|2000 Summer}} {{abbrv|{{color|red|DSQ}}|Disqualified}} || −1 || || || −1
| rowspan=11 align=left | American [[Marion Jones]] was stripped of her three gold and two bronze medals by the [[International Olympic Committee]] (IOC), after confessing that she had taken the [[anabolic steroid]] [[tetrahydrogestrinone]] before competing in Sydney.<ref>{{cite news|last=Shipley|first=Amy|title=Marion Jones Admits to Steroid Use|newspaper=The Washington Post|date=5 October 2007|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/content/article/2007/10/04/AR2007100401666_pf.html|access-date=8 March 2010|archive-date=28 June 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110628214312/http://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/content/article/2007/10/04/AR2007100401666_pf.html|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://nbcsports.msnbc.com/id/22170098/|title=IOC strips Jones of all 5 Olympic medals|date=12 December 2007|agency=Associated Press|publisher=MSNBC|access-date=8 March 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080218091719/http://nbcsports.msnbc.com/id/22170098/|archive-date=18 February 2008|url-status=dead}}</ref><br>The [[Athletics at the 2000 Summer Olympics – Women's 100 metres|women's 100 metres]] gold medal has not been reallocated, because the presumed recipient, [[Ekaterini Thanou]] of [[Greece at the 2000 Summer Olympics|Greece]], was given a two-year ban for doping just before the [[2004 Summer Olympics]]. After years of deliberations the IOC decided to upgrade third- and fourth-placed athletes to silver and bronze, while not upgrading Thanou.<br>Jones' teammates on the relay teams had their medals reinstated due to the fact that, according to the rules at the time, a team should not be stripped of a medal because of a doping offense by one athlete.<ref>{{cite news|title=US relay runners win Olympic medals appeal|date=16 July 2010|first=Graham|last=Dunbar|agency=Associated Press}}</ref>

| rowspan=4 align=left | On 2 August 2008, the IOC stripped the gold medal from the U.S. [[Athletics at the 2000 Summer Olympics – Men's 4 × 400 metres relay|men's 4 x 400-metre relay team]] after [[Antonio Pettigrew]] admitted to taking [[Erythropoietin|EPO]]. The IOC reallocated the gold, silver and bronze medals to the teams from [[Nigeria at the 2000 Summer Olympics|Nigeria]], [[Jamaica at the 2000 Summer Olympics|Jamaica]] and [[Bahamas at the 2020 Summer Olympics|the Bahamas]], respectively.<ref>{{cite news |title=IOC Executive Board meets ahead of London Games |url=http://www.olympic.org/news/ioc-executive-board-meets-ahead-of-london-games/168640 |publisher=International Olympic Committee |date=21 July 2012 |access-date=3 August 2012 |archive-date=28 July 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130728233441/http://www.olympic.org/news/ioc-executive-board-meets-ahead-of-london-games/168640 |url-status=live }}</ref>

! scope="rowgroup" rowspan=2 | 25 February 2010
| rowspan=2 | [[Gymnastics at the 2000 Summer Olympics|Gymnastics]], [[Gymnastics at the 2000 Summer Olympics – Women's artistic team all-around|Women's artistic team all-around]]
| align=left | {{flagIOCathlete|[[Dong Fangxiao]]|CHN|2000 Summer}} {{abbrv|{{color|red|DSQ}}|Disqualified}} || || || −1 || −1
| rowspan=2 align=left | On 25 February 2010, the ''[[Associated Press]]'' reported that one of the members of the Chinese Gymnastic team was found to be under the minimum age limit set for competition. The governing body of the event, the [[International Gymnastics Federation]] (FIG), reported that it determined [[Dong Fangxiao]] to be 14 during the 2000 Olympics. The minimum age for competition was 16. The FIG invalidated the results of the competition in relation to the disqualified athlete. On 28 April 2010, the International Olympic Committee formally stripped the Chinese team of its bronze medal in the team event. The United States, which originally placed fourth, was awarded the bronze.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://nbcsports.msnbc.com/id/35610686/ns/sports-olympic_sports/ |title=Chinese may forfeit 2000 gymnastics bronze |date=26 February 2010 |agency=Associated Press|work=NBC Sports |access-date=8 March 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100301091311/http://nbcsports.msnbc.com/id/35610686/ns/sports-olympic_sports/ |archive-date=1 March 2010 |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://nbcsports.msnbc.com/id/35610686/ns/sports-olympic_sports/ |title=IOC strips 2000 Games bronze medal from China |date=28 April 2010 |agency=Associated Press|work=USA Today |access-date=8 March 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100301091311/http://nbcsports.msnbc.com/id/35610686/ns/sports-olympic_sports/ |archive-date=1 March 2010 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

| align=left | {{flagIOCathlete|[[Lance Armstrong]]|USA|2000 Summer}} {{abbrv|{{color|red|DSQ}}|Disqualified}} || || || −1 || −1
| rowspan=1 align=left | On 17 January 2013, American [[cycle sport|cyclist]] [[Lance Armstrong]] was stripped of his [[Cycling at the 2000 Summer Olympics – Men's road time trial|bronze medal]] from the [[2000 Summer Olympics]] by the IOC after his confession of being involved in using [[Lance Armstrong doping case|doping]].<ref>{{cite web|title=IOC Statement on Lance Armstrong|url=http://www.olympic.org/news/ioc-statement-on-lance-armstrong/188433|publisher=[[International Olympic Committee]]|date=17 January 2013|access-date=21 January 2013|archive-date=25 December 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181225174242/https://www.olympic.org/news/ioc-statement-on-lance-armstrong|url-status=live}}</ref> The IOC also decided not to award [[Spain at the 2000 Summer Olympics|Spanish]] cyclist [[Abraham Olano]] the bronze medal, as he had also tested positive for doping, back in 1998.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/lance-armstrong-stripped-of-olympic-bronze-medal/|title=Lance Armstrong stripped of Olympic bronze medal|website=[[CBS News]] |date=17 January 2013 |access-date=10 March 2020|archive-date=5 April 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200405210329/https://www.cbsnews.com/news/lance-armstrong-stripped-of-olympic-bronze-medal/|url-status=live}}</ref>
